name: Seat Board
note: The wooden board a longcase clock's movement rests on.
tip: Hold X as your hand sweeps past a dot to swing onto it. Each swing reverses your spin.

name: Fusee
note: A cone-shaped pulley that evens out a mainspring's pull as it unwinds.
tip: Translucent dots are bonus dots: 1,000 for the first, 2,000 for the next, up to 5,000 each.

name: Foliot
note: The weighted bar that regulated the earliest verge-escapement clocks.
tip: Hold Shift to flip: you grab the dot and keep spinning the same way.

name: Hipp-Toggle
note: An electrical contact that kicks a pendulum only when its swing starts to fade.
tip: Hold Z to bounce off a dot and reverse without moving. Walls always bounce you.

name: Invar
note: A nickel-steel alloy that barely grows with heat, prized for pendulum rods.
tip: Enemy hands destroy yours on contact. Watch the blue hand's rhythm before you move.

name: Beat Setting
note: Adjusting a clock so its tick and tock are even.
tip: Bonus dots stack up: 1,000, 2,000 and so on, to 5,000 each.

name: Rack
note: The toothed arc that counts the hour in rack striking.
tip: Watch each enemy's rhythm before your first key; the clock waits.

name: Ting-Tang
note: Quarters struck on two bells of different pitch.
tip: Bonus dots stack up: 1,000, 2,000 and so on, to 5,000 each.

name: Rise and Fall
note: A regulator that raises or lowers the pendulum from the dial.
tip: Watch each enemy's rhythm before your first key; the clock waits.

name: Fly
note: The air brake that sets the speed of a striking train.
tip: Watch each enemy's rhythm before your first key; the clock waits.

name: Rating Nut
note: The knurled nut under a pendulum bob, turned to make the clock gain or lose.
tip: Spikes only hurt you. Sweep over an hourglass for 10 more seconds and 1,000 points.

name: Stackfreed
note: A spring-loaded cam that evened out early mainsprings, before the fusee.
tip: Grab the way station (diamond). If you die, you restart there with the time you had. Hard has none.

name: Free Pendulum
note: A pendulum that does no work, only keeps time.
tip: Way stations save your place and your time. Hard has none.

name: Cannon Pinion
note: The tube that carries the minute hand and slips for setting.
tip: Spikes sit between dots. Pick a spin that sweeps away from them.

name: Crank Key
note: A winding key with a handle for heavy springs.
tip: Hourglasses add 10 seconds and 1,000 points.

name: Strike Train
note: The gear train that drives the hour strike.
tip: Way stations save your place and your time. Hard has none.

name: Strike/Silent
note: The lever that turns a clock's strike on or off.
tip: Spikes sit between dots. Pick a spin that sweeps away from them.

name: Suspension Spring
note: The thin spring a pendulum hangs from.
tip: Hourglasses add 10 seconds and 1,000 points.

name: Wheel Train
note: The chain of gears that carries power from spring or weight to the escapement.
tip: Way stations save your place and your time. Hard has none.

name: Rhomboid
note: A pendulum whose rod is a diamond-shaped frame.
tip: Spikes sit between dots. Pick a spin that sweeps away from them.

name: Repeating Work
note: The mechanism that lets a watch chime the time whenever you ask.
tip: While you ride a slowdown dot (triangle), every enemy hand runs at half speed.

name: Crown Wheel
note: The saw-toothed wheel that drives a verge escapement.
tip: Moving spikes orbit dots like clock hands, at the middle of an invisible hand.

name: Hour Wheel
note: The wheel that carries the hour hand.
tip: Moving spikes orbit at the middle of an invisible hand.

name: Escapement
note: The part that lets the gear train advance one tooth at a time.
tip: Walls bounce you. Use them to turn around without a dot.

name: Banking Pins
note: The stops that limit a pallet fork's swing.
tip: Ride a slowdown dot to halve every enemy's speed.

name: Spandrel
note: The corner ornament on a square clock dial.
tip: Moving spikes orbit at the middle of an invisible hand.

name: Hairspring
note: The fine spiral spring that makes a balance wheel swing back.
tip: Walls bounce you. Use them to turn around without a dot.

name: Shortt Clock
note: A free-pendulum clock accurate to about a second a year.
tip: Ride a slowdown dot to halve every enemy's speed.

name: Pillars
note: The posts that hold a movement's plates apart.
tip: Moving spikes orbit at the middle of an invisible hand.

name: Motion Work
note: The gears that give a 12 to 1 reduction from minute to hour hand.
tip: Walls bounce you. Use them to turn around without a dot.

name: Count Wheel
note: A notched wheel that counts out the blows of the strike.
tip: Pass any hand over a switch to open or close the door with the same colour and dots.

name: Warning Wheel
note: The wheel that holds the strike ready just before the hour.
tip: Ring dots vanish when you let go of them, and come back after a moment.

name: Brocot
note: A visible French escapement with semicircular jewelled pallets.
tip: Switches flip doors of the same colour and dots. Don't get caught in a moving door.

name: Balance Wheel
note: The oscillating wheel that keeps time in watches and carriage clocks.
tip: Ring dots vanish behind you. Plan the way back.

name: Tic-Tac
note: A tiny anchor escapement spanning only two teeth.
tip: Switches flip doors of the same colour and dots. Don't get caught in a moving door.

name: Going Barrel
note: A spring barrel that keeps driving while it is wound.
tip: Ring dots vanish behind you. Plan the way back.

name: Platform
note: A self-contained escapement mounted on top of a carriage clock.
tip: Switches flip doors of the same colour and dots. Don't get caught in a moving door.

name: Impulse Pin
note: The jewel the pallet fork strikes to keep the balance going.
tip: Switches flip doors of the same colour and dots. Don't get caught in a moving door.

name: Balance Staff
note: The axle of a watch's balance wheel.
tip: Switches flip doors of the same colour and dots. Don't get caught in a moving door.

name: Roller Table
note: The disc on the balance staff carrying the impulse pin.
tip: Ring dots vanish behind you. Plan the way back.

name: Barrel
note: The brass drum that houses a clock's mainspring.
tip: Grabbing a hyperdot sends you to its twin with the same angle and spin.

name: Detent
note: The chronometer escapement, freeing the balance for most of its swing.
tip: Death dots (squares) are safe to ride, but jumping straight from one to another kills you.

name: Guard Pin
note: The pin that keeps a pallet fork from slipping out of action.
tip: Shield dots (rings) make you immune to enemy hands while you stay on them.

name: Bushing
note: A brass sleeve fitted where a pivot hole has worn.
tip: Hyperdots carry you to their twin with the same angle and spin.

name: Contrate
note: The crown-shaped wheel that turns the drive through a right angle.
tip: Never jump straight from one death dot to another.

name: Bezel
note: The ring that holds the glass over a dial.
tip: On a shield dot, enemy hands pass through you.

name: Verge
note: The earliest mechanical escapement, with two pallets on an upright staff.
tip: Hyperdots carry you to their twin with the same angle and spin.

name: Duplex
note: An escapement with two sets of teeth on one escape wheel.
tip: Never jump straight from one death dot to another.

name: Regulator
note: A precision clock used to set other clocks.
tip: On a shield dot, enemy hands pass through you.

name: Potence
note: The bracket that holds the lower pivot of a verge.
tip: Hyperdots carry you to their twin with the same angle and spin.

name: Lantern Pinion
note: A pinion made of wires between two discs, like a lantern.
tip: Moving dots travel one place every quarter turn. Ride one across the gap.

name: Gridiron
note: A pendulum of brass and steel rods that cancel out heat expansion.
tip: An extended dot is one long dot: stay on it and you slide from end to end.

name: Escape Wheel
note: The last wheel of the train, released by the escapement.
tip: Moving dots arrive on the grid every quarter turn. Time your grab.

name: Endless Chain
note: Huygens' loop of chain that lets one weight drive while being wound.
tip: Extended dots carry you from end to end while you spin.

name: Pallet
note: The nib on the anchor that the escape wheel pushes against.
tip: Moving dots arrive on the grid every quarter turn. Time your grab.

name: Cylinder
note: A watch escapement built around a hollow cut-away cylinder.
tip: Extended dots carry you from end to end while you spin.

name: Seconds Bit
note: The small subsidiary dial for the seconds hand.
tip: Moving dots arrive on the grid every quarter turn. Time your grab.

name: Pivot Hole
note: The bearing in which a pivot runs.
tip: Extended dots carry you from end to end while you spin.

name: Rack Hook
note: The arm acting as a click for the rack in rack-striking clocks.
tip: Moving dots arrive on the grid every quarter turn. Time your grab.

name: Remontoire
note: A small spring rewound at intervals to give even power.
tip: Extended dots carry you from end to end while you spin.

name: Oil Sink
note: The depression around a pivot hole that holds oil.
tip: Oil globs wake when you pass over them, then hunt you dot by dot. Never grab a dot one sits on.

name: Click
note: The pawl that stops a wound spring from running back.
tip: Oil globs wake when you touch them and drip toward you, sometimes splitting in two.

name: Grasshopper
note: Harrison's nearly frictionless escapement with hinged pallets.
tip: Oil globs wake when you touch them and drip toward you, sometimes splitting in two.

name: Moonphase
note: A rotating disc that shows the phase of the moon.
tip: Oil globs wake when you touch them and drip toward you, sometimes splitting in two.

name: Shock Setting
note: A sprung jewel mount that protects the balance pivots.
tip: Oil globs wake when you touch them and drip toward you, sometimes splitting in two.

name: Pendulum Bob
note: The weight at the bottom of a pendulum rod.
tip: Oil globs wake when you touch them and drip toward you, sometimes splitting in two.

name: Sidereal Time
note: Time measured against the stars, not the sun.
tip: Oil globs wake when you touch them and drip toward you, sometimes splitting in two.

name: Pin Wheel
note: An escapement whose wheel carries pins instead of teeth.
tip: Oil globs wake when you touch them and drip toward you, sometimes splitting in two.

name: Anchor
note: An escapement shaped like a ship's anchor, rocking with the pendulum.
tip: Oil globs wake when you touch them and drip toward you, sometimes splitting in two.

name: Lenticular Bob
note: A lens-shaped pendulum bob.
tip: Oil globs wake when you touch them and drip toward you, sometimes splitting in two.

name: Bolt and Shutter
note: Maintaining power that covers the winding holes until engaged.
tip: Pass over the lighter to start the fuse. Stay clear of the spark and the blast; the bomb breaks walls.

name: Hog's Bristle
note: The bristle regulator used on the earliest balance clocks.
tip: Sweep past a wallbuster to push it. It smashes the first wall it hits, then comes back.

name: Deadbeat
note: An escapement whose escape wheel does not recoil at each tick.
tip: Light the fuse, then keep clear: the blast breaks walls and kills hands.

name: Kidney Piece
note: The cam in an equation clock used to show solar time.
tip: Push a wallbuster with the side of your hand to smash a wall.

name: Pinion Leaves
note: The teeth of the small driven gears in a clock's train.
tip: Light the fuse, then keep clear: the blast breaks walls and kills hands.

name: Lunette
note: A crescent-shaped bezel or dial opening.
tip: Push a wallbuster with the side of your hand to smash a wall.

name: Balance Cock
note: The bracket that holds the top pivot of the balance.
tip: Light the fuse, then keep clear: the blast breaks walls and kills hands.

name: Lever
note: The escapement in most mechanical watches, with a pallet fork.
tip: Push a wallbuster with the side of your hand to smash a wall.

name: Synchronome
note: An electric master clock that drives slave dials.
tip: Light the fuse, then keep clear: the blast breaks walls and kills hands.

name: Compensation
note: Any device that corrects a timekeeper for temperature.
tip: Push a wallbuster with the side of your hand to smash a wall.

name: Hammer
note: The arm that strikes the bell or gong.
tip: Any hand crossing a trigger fires every gun of its colour. Bullets stop only at walls.

name: Lifting Piece
note: The lever that the motion work raises to start the strike.
tip: Up/down switches raise or sink every dot with the same symbol. Don't be on one when it sinks.

name: Bimetallic Balance
note: A balance rim of two metals that flexes with heat.
tip: Up/down switches raise and sink every dot with their symbol.

name: Pull Repeat
note: A cord that makes a clock strike the last hour again.
tip: Up/down switches raise and sink every dot with their symbol.

name: Stopwork
note: The mechanism that stops a mainspring being overwound.
tip: Triggers fire every gun of their colour, whoever crosses them.

name: Equation of Time
note: The difference between sundial time and clock time.
tip: Up/down switches raise and sink every dot with their symbol.

name: Hoop Wheel
note: The wheel with a hoop that locks a count-wheel strike.
tip: Triggers fire every gun of their colour, whoever crosses them.

name: Crutch
note: The arm that passes the escapement's push to the pendulum.
tip: Up/down switches raise and sink every dot with their symbol.

name: Isochronism
note: Swinging in equal time whatever the size of the swing.
tip: Triggers fire every gun of their colour, whoever crosses them.

name: Passing Strike
note: A single blow on the hour, without counting.
tip: Up/down switches raise and sink every dot with their symbol.

name: Chronometer
note: A clock accurate enough to find longitude at sea.
tip: Moving dots arrive on the grid every quarter turn. Time your grab.

name: Ratchet
note: The toothed wheel the click holds while the clock is wound.
tip: Extended dots carry you from end to end while you spin.

name: Gathering Pallet
note: The piece that gathers the rack one tooth per blow.
tip: Up/down switches raise and sink every dot with their symbol.

name: Arch Dial
note: A dial with a semicircular top above the square face.
tip: Switches flip doors of the same colour and dots. Don't get caught in a moving door.

name: Chapter Ring
note: The ring of hour numerals on a dial.
tip: Extended dots carry you from end to end while you spin.

name: Mercury Jar
note: A pendulum bob filled with mercury to correct for temperature.
tip: Up/down switches raise and sink every dot with their symbol.

name: Arbor
note: The axle that carries a wheel and its pinion.
tip: Up/down switches raise and sink every dot with their symbol.

name: Tourbillon
note: A rotating cage that averages out gravity's pull on the balance.
tip: Up/down switches raise and sink every dot with their symbol.

name: Mainspring
note: The coiled spring that powers a clock or watch.
tip: Switches flip doors of the same colour and dots. Don't get caught in a moving door.

name: Snail
note: A spiral-stepped cam that decides how many blows a rack-striking clock sounds.
tip: Two ways to the goal. The way station is guarded; the right-hand column is spiked.
